title: Recall Gateway: small-user-cache proto / rough PRD
content:
Quick context:
- Idea sketch for a tiny, policy-driven Recall Gateway (RG) that lives between our API and model runtime. Purpose: provide fast per-user/session recall for short-term signals (last N turns, pinned snippets, embeddings), with configurable gating/eviction policies so product teams can trade latency/cost/privacy without touching model code.

Problem statement / motivation:
- Many apps need rapid, cheap recall for very small working sets (e.g., last 3 turns + 2 saved notes). Hitting main KV or vector DB for every request adds latency and cost.
- Current options: (a) put everything into model prompt (expensive), (b) rely on client to re-send context (fragile), (c) use centralized vector DB (higher tail latency + cold misses).
- We need a middle ground: ephemeral, local-ish cache that can answer common recall queries (<100KB per user) in ~5ms median and supports simple ranking/filtering.

Goals (measurable):
- 95th percentile recall latency < 15ms for cache hits (p95 measured at API side).
- Reduce persistent-store read rate for short-window context by 60% for participating routes.
- Expose policy controls to product teams: window size (tokens/items), TTL, sample-for-embedding, privacy mode (no-persist).

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for long-term vector DBs (Pinecone/Weaviate) or full session store.
- Not a single-source-of-truth for analytics.

Stakeholders:
- eng-serving-runtime (owner), product-hosted-api (primary consumers), privacy/compliance, SRE (scaling/ops), devexp (SDK ergonomics).

User stories (rough):
- As a chat product engineer, I want the gateway to surface the last 3 turns and a pinned user note to the model without doing a DB read on every request, so my median response latency drops by ~30ms and cost per request is lower.
- As a platform operator, I want per-tenant/global policies + telemetry so I can shut off persistent caching for regulated tenants.
- As an experimentation owner, I want flaggable staging so I can A/B the gateway on 10% of traffic for a route.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- RG accepts a lightweight envelope from API indicating user_id, route, flags (e.g., include_last_k=3, privacy=private), returns concatenated snippets + optional embedding vector.
- Basic eviction policy: per-user LRU by item count with configurable max-items (default 10).
- Durable cold store fallback: on miss, fetch from session store then populate cache asynchronously.
- Admin dashboard: per-route hit/miss rates, avg latency, storage footprint.

High-level design options:
1) In-process gateway: RG as a thin process inside API nodes (fastest, single-tenant memory), but complicates autoscaling + state reassignment.
2) Shared service with sharded in-memory caches (e.g., memcached-like) colocated in region — tradeoffs: network hop but simpler to scale.
3) Hybrid edge-first: client SDK can keep a small volatile cache; RG as authoritative aggregator.

Implementation sketch (preferred: 2 hybrid):
- RG fronted by HTTP/gRPC. Request path: API -> RG -> (cache hit) -> return; (miss) -> RG -> session-store (or vector DB) -> return + async populate.
- Shard key: tenant_id + user_id low-entropy hash to pick node. TTLs are soft; eviction performed LRU with occasional background compaction.
- Item model: {item_id, kind: [turn, note, embed], created_at, last_access, size_bytes, score_meta}. Keep types small (text up to 2KB; embeddings up to 1KB).
- Ranking on response: simple recency-weighted score; product can specify prefer:pins, prefer:semantic-match (expensive).

API surface (proto-ish):
- POST /recall/query {tenant_id, user_id, route, policy: {max_items, include_types, privacy_mode}, query_text?, return_embeddings:false} -> {items: [text...], embeddings?: [...], hit: boolean, meta: {hit_rate_est}}
- POST /recall/patch {tenant_id, user_id, items: [{id, type, payload}], ttl?} -> 200
- Admin endpoints: /recall/config, /recall/metrics, /recall/evict

Telemetry / metrics:
- per-route/user hit/miss, median p50/p95/duration of recall queries, persistent-store fallthroughs, avg items per user, memory usage per shard, eviction rate.
- Correlate recall-hit with model-latency and token usage (cost reduction estimate).

Privacy & compliance considerations:
- Default: do not persist items to long-term storage unless tenant opts in. Provide "no-write" privacy_mode.
- Encryption at rest for in-memory dump/backups. Control plane must support tenant-level disable. Audit logs for reads when privacy flags set.

Operational considerations & SRE:
- Capacity: expected small item per-user footprint; still worst-case mulit-tenant hot keys -> implement request-rate limiting, per-user caps.
- Failure modes: RG unavailable -> API must fall back to session-store read path (higher latency but safe). Ensure circuit-breaker with backoff.
- Rolling deploy: start on low-traffic region, enable feature-flag per-route.

Experiment plan / rollout:
- Phase 0 (lab): local dev harness + integration tests (unit + perf) — 2 weeks.
- Phase 1 (dogfood): internal product team opt-in for 1 route, 5% traffic, collect telemetry — 3 weeks.
- Phase 2: increase to 25% with canary autoscaling rules + SLO monitoring — 4 weeks.
- Phase 3: open for platform teams with docs + SDK helper — 2–3 weeks.

Metrics to watch during experiments:
- Recall hit rate, fallback DB qps, added latency p50/p95 from RG, memory footprint, cost delta per 1k requests.

Open questions / tradeoffs (TODO):
- Embedding handling: store embeddings in RG? Storing and querying semantically at gateway is heavier; consider only storing text and providing on-demand embedding generation.
- Cross-device replay: how to keep small caches consistent when user uses multiple devices? Option: make RG per-tenant multi-region with replication (complex) or accept slightly higher miss rate.
- Tenant isolation: per-tenant dedicated pools for enterprise customers vs shared pools with strict quotas.
- Cold-start strategy: prefetch recent items during session creation vs lazy fill on first request. Which reduces latency more for our traffic pattern? (Need synthetic tests).

Short-term next actions (for me / Mike / Mika):
- [ ] Prototype sharded service using hash ring + local LRU store (POC repo skeleton). (owner: me)
- [ ] Add simple perf harness that simulates 1M users with small working sets, measure p95. (owner: Mika)
- [ ] Draft SDK helpers for product-hosted-api to toggle policies per-route (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Create perf JIRA: INFR-2049 (linked).

Notes to self / heuristics:
- Keep API minimal. Complexity hides in policies not surface shape.
- Start with text-only items; embeddings can be an opt-in addon.
- Default max-items=10, default TTL=20m seems reasonable for chat flows.

Random brainlets / fringe ideas (capture here):
- Probabilistic sampling: store only a probabilistic sample of past turns to keep costs bounded while preserving high-signal turns (e.g., store turns with 1-in-k sampling but always keep pinned ones).
- Warmup pipeline: when a user is active, a background job streams recent persistent-store items into RG across likely shards so first few interactions are hits.
- Soft-hedged recall: query RG and persistent store in parallel (hedging) for p95 reduction if RG latency is variable — careful: increases backend load.

References / related docs:
- session-eviction-playbook (internal)
- token-batching-hierarchy-journal (perf notes)

Unresolved: need to sync with privacy team on audit log volume and retention for gateway reads.

End of sketch. This is intentionally messy — want quick feedback on the mental model before I formalize into a PRD.
